title: Post-Selection-Free Quantum Automated Learning
abstract: Quantum automated learning (QAL) trains quantum models by directly updating quantum states, offering an approach to quantum machine learning that avoids optimizing variational circuit parameters. However, post-selection constrains the probability of obtaining the final learned model. We develop a post-selection-free QAL algorithm that organizes a complete training path into a coherent quantum circuit and uses fixed-point amplitude amplification to increase the probability of obtaining the learned model. We provide theoretical guarantees on output error and learning loss, and identify conditions under which additional coherent resources reduce the cost of restarting failed trajectories. The construction gives QAL a coherent implementation with explicit learning guarantees and resource costs, enabling a model with certified learning quality and controlled output error to be obtained with high probability.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, post-selection-free algorithm for Quantum Automated Learning (QAL) that trains quantum models by encoding the entire learning path into a single coherent quantum circuit. By employing fixed-point amplitude amplification, the method achieves high-probability guarantees on both the learned model's quality and the associated resource costs. This work significantly advances the theoretical feasibility of implementing robust quantum machine learning protocols.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of Quantum Automated Learning (QAL) by developing a method that eliminates the need for post-selection, which typically constrains the probability of obtaining the learned quantum model.
main_result: A post-selection-free QAL algorithm is proposed that organizes the entire training path into a coherent quantum circuit, using fixed-point amplitude amplification to achieve high-probability learning guarantees.
method: The core method involves using fixed-point amplitude amplification (FPAA) on a coherent circuit representation of the training path, which is built using unitary dilations and flag qubits.
model_or_system: The model is Quantum Automated Learning (QAL), which trains quantum models by directly updating quantum states via projector-mixing updates, avoiding variational parameter optimization.

Figure 3: Exact circuit checks of amplification and branch preservation. The good-flag probability increases while the successful model retains the conditional QAL output to numerical precision.

Figure 2: Normalized imaginary-time evolution of a six- site Ising chain. Panel (a) shows the energy error; (b) plots the same trajectory against schematic primitive- call costs for three success-management methods. Local RUS uses the actual success probability, QAA assumes it is known, and FPAA uses the spectral floor.

Figure 4: Two ways to execute a predeclared QAL path. Measured global restart discards a failed partial path; coherent execution retains the flags until fixed-point am- plification acts on their joint success space. The good branch has the exact conditional QAL model. Discard- ing all flags gives an approximate unconditioned model, under the stated preparation and reflection access as- sumptions.

Figure 5: Per-accepted-output FPAA-to-global-restart cost ratios. The upper panel counts selected-filter queries; the lower adds weighted preparation, reflection, flag, measurement, reset, and readout charges. Ratios below one occur in the weighted model. Each compari- son uses conditional accepted outputs and the specified cost assignments.
